_meta.indication: For the treatment of adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) caused by susceptible microorganisms including S. pneumoniae, MSSA, H. influenzae, L. pneumophila, M. pneumoniae, and C. pneumoniae

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-control (moxifloxacin), noninferiority; lefamulin 150 mg IV q12h for at least 3 days with optional switch to 600 mg PO q12h
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with PORT III-V CABP
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with Early Clinical Response at 96 +/- 24 hours after the first dose of study drug in the ITT population
pivotal_trials.result: ECR rate 87.3% lefamulin vs 90.2% moxifloxacin; difference -2.9% (95% CI, -8.5% to 2.8%) — noninferior

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-control (moxifloxacin), noninferiority; lefamulin 600 mg PO q12h for 5 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with PORT II-IV CABP
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with Early Clinical Response at 96 +/- 24 hours after the first dose of study drug in the ITT population
pivotal_trials.result: ECR rate 90.8% lefamulin vs 90.8% moxifloxacin; difference 0% (95% CI, -4.4% to 4.5%) — noninferior

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%): XENLETA Injection — administration site reactions, hepatic enzyme elevation, nausea, hypokalemia, insomnia, headache; XENLETA Tablets — diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, hepatic enzyme elevation. Diarrhea occurred in 12.2% of oral lefamulin subjects vs 1.1% of oral moxifloxacin. IV administration site reactions occurred in 7.3% of lefamulin vs 2.6% of moxifloxacin subjects. QT prolongation is a warning.
target_moa: Lefamulin is a pleuromutilin antibacterial that inhibits prokaryotic ribosomal protein synthesis by binding to the peptidyl transferase center (PTC) at the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome

rems.type: No REMS needed; risks may be adequately managed in the postmarketing setting through labeling

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion

summary.text: XENLETA (lefamulin) was reviewed under Priority review as an NDA and was granted Fast Track and Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designations for CABP; efficacy was established in two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 noninferiority trials (Studies 3101 and 3102) versus moxifloxacin, and it was approved first cycle without accelerated approval or an advisory committee.

The Applicant has provided substantial evidence of effectiveness of lefamulin for the treatment of CABP due to the designated susceptible bacteria in adults from two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (Studies 3101 and 3102).
